title: hello-crew — three roles, one baton (target: crew)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “Three named roles take turns under one shared session, each with its own instructions.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: three roles, one entry

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape, pick who starts
beats.cue: “entry: picks which role takes the first message — no ‘who goes first’ negotiation.”

beats.label: Scope permissions once, for the whole crew
beats.cue: Permissions are crew-level: every role runs under the same block, not three copies.

beats.label: Role 1 · the researcher
beats.cue: “List 3 concise risks… then call the Handoff tool with target="writer".” It hands off, it doesn't write.

beats.label: Role 2 · the writer
beats.cue: “Write a single 4-sentence summary post” — and it may SendMessage the critic mid-turn.

beats.label: Role 3 · the critic
beats.cue: “Give a one-sentence direct answer. Be terse.” The peer that answers, never the one that ships.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the crew well-formedness passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Three roles lowered to JSON — same model, empty tool lists. The instructions are the only thing that varies.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target crew (3 roles, entry researcher); every role carries the inherited claude-sonnet-5 and "tools": []

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no key in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the daemon's stdin input gate

beats.label: Open the emitted orchestrator
beats.cue: “Sixteen lines: three roles registered, one entry set. The routing is the runtime's job.”

beats.label: Open one role
beats.cue: “One file per role — the researcher's instructions, verbatim. And `tools: []`. Nothing here declares Handoff.”

beats.label: So where does Handoff come from?
beats.cue: “Not the spec, not the bundle — the crew runtime hands every role a Handoff and a SendMessage to each peer, and pre-allows both.”

verify.note: the installed crew-orchestrator imports both tool factories, pre-allows both patterns, and composeRoleTools builds them per role — which is why every role's declared tool list is empty

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A crew isn't a chat — the CLI names the shapes it takes.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "crew")`

beats.label: Boot the daemon with nothing to say
beats.cue: “The daemon takes a topic on stdin. No input, no turn — it says so and exits 2.”

verify.note: designed refusal — `[crew] no input on stdin`, exit 2; deps were installed by the --check beat

beats.label: Hand the crew a topic
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Researcher lists three risks, hands the baton to the writer, writer pings the critic.” tee keeps the stream.
beats.command: echo "Topic: rolling out vector-search to production" | bun live/dist/daemon.ts | tee live/run.jsonl

verify.note: three model calls minimum, four if the writer asks the critic; needs Anthropic credentials. tee keeps the event stream so the next group needs no second run

groups.title: One more thing · every baton pass is an event

beats.label: Read the run back as events
beats.cue: [needs-key] Every crew event was one JSON line on stdout — the baton passes, in order, replayed from the file we kept.

verify.note: the run the previous beat teed, projected to its event kind stream — no second daemon process and no second charge; needs jq on PATH and live/run.jsonl from run-topic

beats.label: Three roles, one session file
beats.cue: [needs-key] The durable transcript is one file per run — every role activation inside it, in baton order.

verify.note: the session JSONL only exists after a real run; the crew shares one RunContext per run, so all three roles append to a single sess_<hex>.jsonl — a second run writes a second file
